channel.title: HTTP on Humus
channel.description: Recent content in HTTP on Humus

item.title: Migrating from Echo
item.description:
This guide moves a small Echo v5 service to humus. Its first step runs the Echo engine on humus, so the process, settings, TLS, telemetry, probes and shutdown are humus’s from then on. Its next steps move the routes onto openapi/v3 a few at a time, while Echo serves the rest, until the service no longer requires Echo.

Two things make that work. An Echo engine is an http.Handler, which httpserver.NewService serves. And an openapi.API hands every request no operation serves to its Unmatched handlers, which can be the Echo engine.

item.title: Migrating from Fiber
item.description:
This guide moves a small Fiber v3 service to humus. Its first step runs the Fiber app on humus, so the process, settings, TLS, telemetry, probes and shutdown are humus’s from then on. Its next steps move the routes onto openapi/v3 a few at a time, while Fiber serves the rest, until the service requires neither Fiber nor fasthttp.

Fiber runs on fasthttp, not net/http, so each handler is rewritten when its route moves. Two things still let the service move a few routes at a time. Fiber’s adaptor middleware serves a Fiber app as an http.HandlerFunc, which httpserver.NewService serves. And an openapi.API hands every request no operation serves to its Unmatched handlers, which can be the adapted app.
